long_description:
Family Shiny with Kris - Akatarawa Forest
Registrations open NOW

What to expect

This is a “Family Shiny” trip into the Akatarawa Forest.

Non members are welcome to join us but must register to obtain details of start time and location.

Vehicles must have a low ratio gearbox and must not be a 4wd car, station wagon or van, and if a soft top must have a roll cage.

Visitor Registration- $20.00 per driver
There is no trip fee for this trip however non-members pay a “Day Membership Fee” of $20. This is payable in Cash to the Trip Leader on the day.

The trip should be relatively easy as it needs to cater for people just starting out and all types of 4wd vehicles – but a good way to see if you want to get into 4wding and a chance to meet some of our club members (if you are unsure if your vehicle is suitable just ask).

No Dogs Allowed sorry

Once you have completed 3 Family Shinys you can join the club but can only participate in Family Shiny or Touring Class trips. Once you have also done a Training Day and had your vehicle inspected by one of our approved inspectors you can come along on our other more adventurous trips. To find out more on how to join our club go to https://ccvcwellington.wildapricot.org/page-1725861.

Like our Facebook page to find out about more trips and club nights.

Vietnamese Lunar New Year Festival 2027 | Xuân Hội Ngộ - Tết Xa Mà Gần
Vietnamese Lunar New Year Festival 2027 | Xuân Hội Ngộ – Tết Xa Mà Gần

Make the Most of Your Waitangi Day Long Weekend – Celebrate Tết With Us!

Looking for something fun to do with your family and friends over the long weekend?

Come celebrate the Year of the Goat with Viet Hub NZ! We’re bringing a little piece of Vietnam to Lower Hutt, filled with delicious food, colourful performances, cultural discoveries, hands-on workshops and plenty of festive fun!

Whether you’ve celebrated Tết your whole life or are experiencing Vietnamese Lunar New Year for the first time, everyone is welcome!

Event Details

📅 Monday, 8 February 2027 | Waitangi Day Public Holiday
🕚 11:00 AM – 4:00 PM
📍 Walter Nash Stadium, Taitā, Lower Hutt
🎟️ FREE ENTRY | Family-Friendly | Everyone Welcome!

What’s Happening?

🎶 Live Performances & Entertainment

Enjoy vibrant cultural performances, traditional music, lion dances and amazing local talents bringing the festival to life!

🍜 Vietnamese Street Food & Festival Market

Come hungry! Discover delicious Vietnamese street food, refreshing drinks, sweet treats and exciting local market stalls.

🏮 Explore Vietnam – Cultural Discovery Stations

Take a journey through Vietnam without leaving Wellington! Explore Vietnamese traditions, discover fascinating stories and learn what makes Tết so special.

🎨 Get Creative with Vietnamese Crafts

Create your own festive decorations, try Vietnamese folk painting, make traditional Tết couplets (câu đối) and take home something handmade.

🧧 Traditional Games & Family Fun

Challenge your friends, play Vietnamese traditional games and enjoy interactive activities designed for children and adults alike!

🥢 Hands-on Cooking Workshops

Discover Vietnamese flavours and learn how to make traditional treats through fun cooking experiences. Spaces may be limited.

🌸 New Year Wishes & Traditions

Learn a Vietnamese New Year greeting, write your wishes for the year ahead and discover the beautiful customs behind our celebrations.

🎁 Explore, Collect & Win!

Visit our cultural stations, complete fun activities and collect stamps along the way for a chance to receive a little festive surprise! (While supplies last.)

A Little Piece of Vietnam, Right Here in New Zealand

For Vietnamese families, Tết is more than a celebration. It’s a time to reconnect with family, childhood memories, treasured traditions and the feeling of home.

For our wider New Zealand community, it’s a wonderful opportunity to experience Vietnamese culture through food, stories, creativity and shared experiences.

At Viet Hub NZ, we believe culture is something to be shared, experienced and celebrated together.

You don’t need to be Vietnamese to celebrate Tết. Just bring your curiosity, your appetite and your festive spirit!

Make Your Long Weekend Memorable!

Why stay home this public holiday when you can enjoy a whole day of food, culture, entertainment and family fun?

Bring your whānau, invite your friends and make some beautiful memories together.

Free entry! Register your tickets to help us plan a wonderful festival for everyone.

Food, market purchases and selected workshops may incur additional costs.

Help Us Bring Tết to Life

Our celebration is made possible by passionate volunteers, community partners and generous supporters.

If you’d like to help us bring more cultural experiences, traditional decorations and festive joy to our community, please consider supporting our fundraising campaign:

https://givealittle.co.nz/cause/bring-lunar-new-year-to-life-a-celebration

Every contribution, big or small, helps us share the joy of Tết!

⸻

Xuân Hội Ngộ 2027 – Tết Xa Mà Gần

Together for Tết, No Matter How Far From Home!

See you this Waitangi Day long weekend at Walter Nash Stadium!

With love,
Viet Hub NZ Team

long_description:
Ha the Unclear - Astigmatic! EP Release Tour
Astigmatic! EP Release Tour.

6 November – Crown Hotel – Ōtepoti | Dunedin *
13 November – Whammy – Tāmaki Makaurau | Auckland *
14 November – Space Academy – Ōtautahi | Christchurch *
4 December – Meow – Pōneke | Wellington ^

* Tickets from undertheradar.co.nz
^ Tickets from meow.nz

In 2024, Ha the Unclear released their amalgam album A Kingdom in a Cul-de-Sac (Think Zik!/Virgin) and played their debut European headline show where they were received warmly by French press and radio, described by FIP as "a kaleidoscopic and surreal pop journey." On their new EP Astigmatic!, the first release since, the band shares five new songs. The lead single 'Cumberland Street (Astigmatic)' extols the joy of hitting a run of green lights on the titular Ōtepoti street. The cry of "Astigmatic!" for which the EP is named, serves as a central optical metaphor; the line "staring at the stars, no they were streetlights leaking in a row" comes, Cathro says, from "a very early memory of pointing out stars to my parents on a Dunedin evening, not realising they were just streetlights on the opposite hill." While 'The Good Times Always End in Tears' is a nostalgia-tinged goodbye-for-now to the old hometown, levity abounds in songs like 'Earth Grazer', a jittery pop number where a missed encounter devolves into a reflection on existential brevity. In the upbeat, frantic 'The Cold', the creative process is likened to gold panning in what must certainly be Gabriel’s Gully or a braided Central Otago river. A meta backing vocal refrain exclaims “the story that I tell myself / the wood with which I build my house.”

The band tours New Zealand across four dates in November and December:

From centuries-old texts to traditional carols given new musical life, this concert explores the many ways composers across different eras and cultures have interpreted the Christmas story.

Our programme brings together music from England to Appalachia, with works by Vaughan Williams, Warlock, Dalglish and Ešenvalds. The music ranges from reflective settings and rich harmonies to lively folk-inspired carols and well-loved Christmas tunes.
And let us know which of your favourite carols you'd like to sing along with us!

Wellington Cathedral of St Paul
2 Hill St, Thorndon

$35/$30 schoolchildren free

long_description:
Timeline - 300 years of music for saxophone
Join us as we explore the history of the saxophone through 300 years of music performed by an exciting yet subtle chamber duo.

This concert explores a broad range of music, from pieces by J.S Bach which predate the saxophone by over 100 years, to modern compositions which push the limits of the instrument. Between these moments you will hear some of the greatest works for saxophone, from the popular showcase Pequeña Czarda to the elegant staple Tableaux de Provence.

Hear the many moods and timbres of the saxophone, from delicately soaring melodies, to dark, enchanting arias and joyful, raucous moments.


Programme:
J.S. Bach - Partita No. 2 for Solo Violin: IV. Gigue
Robert Schumann - 3 Romances
J. B Singelée - Concertino Op. 78
Eugène Bozza - Aria
Pierre Lantier - Sicilienne
Pedro Itturalde - Pequeña Czarda
Paul Bonneau - Caprice en Forme de Valse
Paule Maurice - Tableaux de Provence
Steven Banks - Surrender


$25 pre-sale
$35 door sales
$10 student/concession


About the performers:
Alex Trask is a saxophonist based in Pōneke. He has a keen interest in the classical saxophone and has studied with some of New Zealand's leading player such as Simon Brew and Reuben Chin. He is a member of the Royal New Zealand Air Force Band and has performed with many other significant organizations such as Gallery Orchestra, Saxcess, Wellington Youth Orchestra, and Wellington City Symphonic Band.

Alex is also an accomplished jazz player, and has performed all over the country. In 2026 he appeared with the Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra, as well as playing lead alto for the RNZAF Jazz Orchestra. Alex helf the lead alto chair in the Rodger Fox Big Band from 2024-2025 and has performed as a guest with that band since 2022. In 2026 he recorded his first studio album, which will be released in 2027.


Gabriela Glapska is a Polish-born, Wellington-based pianist celebrated for her expressive artistry, versatility, and collaborative spirit. An accomplished soloist, chamber musician, and sought-after accompanist, she brings clarity, depth, and nuance to a wide range of musical settings.

Gabriela holds a Master’s degree with Distinction from the Feliks Nowowiejski Academy of Music in Bydgoszcz, where she studied under renowned pianist Ewa Pobłocka, and a PhD in Music Performance from Victoria University of Wellington. She currently works as a collaborative pianist at Te Kōkī – New Zealand School of Music.

Whether performing in concert halls, schools, or contemporary music spaces, Gabriela Glapska is known for her refined musicianship, intuitive ensemble playing, and passionate advocacy for music in all its forms.

Photo by Hayden Hockly

name: Tapa: Pacific Histories in Cloth - Art, Making, and Community
venue: 55 Cable Street, Te Aro, New Zealand 6011,Te Papa Tongarewa Museum of NZ, 55 Cable St, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand, Wellington
long_description:
Tapa: Pacific Histories in Cloth - Art, Making, and Community
Join us for a day of making, performance and community activations around tapa, and the bark cloth traditions of the Pacific to celebrate Tapa: Pacific Histories in Cloth, the new pukapuka by Dr Nina Tonga, Dr Rachel Yates Pahulu and Dr Sean Mallon, published by Te Papa Press.

Over generations, people throughout the Pacific have crafted beautiful and practical tapa cloth from the inner bark of various tropical trees. This cloth is known by many names across Te Moana-nui-a-Kiwa – aute in Aotearoa, siapo in Sāmoa, ngatu in Tonga, masi in Fiji, hiapo in Niue, ‘ahu in Tahiti, kapa in Hawai‘i, and many others.

Join us to celebrate Pacific heritage, craft, and Indigenous practice, with renowned tapa makers, knowledge holders, and practitioners for a day of creative making, talanoa, and rich cultural connection.

Drawing on community voices, makers, and artists revitalising the practice across Aotearoa and Te Moana-nui-a-Kiwa, we present an engaging programme honouring the histories, legacies, and living traditions of tapa across the Pacific.

"Tapa: Pacific Histories in Cloth" is the most significant contribution of knowledge about tapa in a generation, offering new views on its practices, meanings and histories across art, dress, culture and curation. This multi authored book draws upon the vast collections of the Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa, illustrating over two hundred tapa from 18 Pacific island nations, from Taiwan to Hawai‘i, to explore its lineages.

Find out more about Tapa: Pacific Histories in Cloth.

name: Catherine Chidgey: The Starving Bride
venue: Hannah Playhouse,12 Cambridge Ter, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand, Wellington
long_description:
Catherine Chidgey: The Starving Bride
Described by the 2026 Arts Foundation Te Tumu Toi Laureate panel as "without a doubt one of New Zealand's most important living writers", internationally bestselling author Catherine Chidgey returns to Verb to discuss her tenth enthralling novel. The Starving Bride is an urgent and searing story set in near-future England.

Dumped by her boyfriend, fired from her job and estranged from her parents, Hazel Whitlock signs up for a sideshow act in Blackpool. The seaside resort has revived all the cancelled old favourites and she will be the Starving Bride. On display in the iconic Blackpool Tower, with a ravenous lion prowling the enclosure, Hazel must lie in silence while strangers view her body.

Join Catherine and Kate Camp for a special one-night event as they discuss the many layers of The Starving Bride, writing female experiences and the questions the book raises about spectacle, desire, survival and society's obsession with beauty.

Unity Books will be at the event bookselling and Catherine will be book signing.

Cover artwork by Max Thompson. Cover design by Todd Atticus. Author photo by Ebony Lamb.

name: AIPA Wellington | The Changing Landscape of Commercial Photography
venue: 2/8 Kent Terrace, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011,8 Kent Ter, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand, Wellington
long_description:
AIPA Wellington | The Changing Landscape of Commercial Photography
The Changing Landscape of Commercial Photography

Expanding the frame to fit the evolving world of image making.
Commercial photography has always evolved alongside technology, creativity and client needs. Today, changes happen faster than ever, the lines between photography, video, motion, stop motion and content creation are increasingly blurred. Agencies and clients are after new ways to tell stories and the expectations and skills in image-making shifts with them.


But what does that actually mean for photographers?


Whether you've spent decades behind the camera, are just finding your feet, or you’re somewhere in between, change always brings questions, sometimes challenges and of course, plenty of opportunities.


So do we need to adapt? What skills are becoming more valuable? How are agencies approaching creative production? And how can we evolve our businesses and creative practice without losing sight of what makes our work distinctive?


On Tuesday 1 December, we’ll unpack these questions and more with our guest speakers:


Ashley Alexander | Photographer, Videographer & Creative
Ashley will share his perspective from behind the camera, how his practice has evolved and the opportunities he's found working across different forms of image-making.


Josh Rollo | Senior Producer, VML
Josh brings the agency perspective, sharing insights into how creative production is changing, what clients are looking for and how agencies are navigating an ever-evolving landscape.


This isn't about having all the answers or trying to be everything to everyone. It's about understanding what's happening around us, learning from each other and recognising the opportunities.


Tuesday 1 December | 6pm

VML, 2/8 Kent Terrace, Mt Victoria, Wellington
Free for AIPA and NZIPP members | $10 for non-members.


Come along and bring your questions, share your experiences and meet other photographers in the industry. Whether you're established, emerging or just curious about what's next, there's a place for you in this conversation.

description:
AIPA Wellington | The Changing Landscape of Commercial Photography The Changing Landscape of Commercial Photography Expanding the frame to fit the evolving world of image making.
Agencies and clients are after new ways to tell stories and the expectations and skills in image-making shifts with them.
Whether you've spent decades behind the camera, are just finding your feet, or you’re somewhere in between, change always brings questions, sometimes challenges and of course, plenty of opportunities.
How are agencies approaching creative production?
This isn't about having all the answers or trying to be everything to everyone.

long_description:
Oh Come All Ye Poprox
On a frosty night just before Christmas, a group of kiwi's away from home in chilly Britain assemble on a neighbourhood street to live out the fantasy they watched in Christmas movies growing up- door to door carolling!

This is a heart-felt, fully improvised narrative Christmas musical from pro company, PopRox once again taking the stage this Christmas at BATS.

Our carollers will create new Christmas songs on the spot as they travel between houses on a quiet English street. Dealing with the cold, their relationships and all those gooey feelings around Christmas, especially when you're far away from home.

It's a heartwarming and hilarious night of improv and Christmas music from your favourite Wellington improv troupe, celebrating their 5th year as a company!

So, grab a delicious Christmas-themed cocktail from the Lumen Bar and settle in for a cozy Christmas with PopRox.

In this season of giving, PopRox has partnered with a bunch of fabulous local artists to create 5 uniquely designed letterboxes to decorate the stage. At the end of the season, these fantastic pieces of art will be up for sale with all proceeds being donated to Wellington City Mission to help families in need this Christmas.

name: Social Media workshop with Samantha Hannah
venue: The Fringe Bar,28 Allen Street, Te Aro, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Social Media workshop with Samantha Hannah
How to get people to your comedy shows using organic social media

A workshop for Wellington comics!

Most of us got into comedy to be funny on stage, not to run a social media account. But these days, getting people along to see you in person usually involves doing a bit of both.

Samantha Hannah (2026 Billy T nominee) is a stand-up comedian at night and a social media specialist by day. She's keen to share what she's learned about using organic social media to sell out shows, and to swap ideas with other comics in Wellington who are doing the same.

This is a relaxed, practical session where we'll chat about:

Ideas of what to post
Leaning into community when posting online
Turning your existing material into clips
Finding a posting rhythm that fits around your busy life and schedule
How to avoid social media burnout
Nurturing and building an audience long before telling them you have a show you want them to come watch!
All levels welcome! Advanced questions can be submitted by sending a DM via fb or Instagram (@samanthahannahcomedy). You’ll also get lots of opportunities to ask questions on the day.

All proceeds go to the Humorous Arts Trust, supporting the 2027 Wellington Raw Comedy Quest.

long_description:
Race of Champions
Eventing is all about trust and partnership �. It is a true my-turn-your-turn bond built on deep mutual respect �. When you truly connect with an animal, it is pure aroha �. I see you �

Yes. For horses it is a shorter time scale Timea Laura Kováčová so horses need to be cared for extremely well,when in your care.. the saying no foot no horse comes to mind.. and the ability in Eventing for the rider to have the skills to be able to say to a well trained horse.. now you have the freedom and sure footedness and training to take the rein at your pace.. but the horses training allows the rider to bring to attention there is a change in course or a jump coming which will need their guidance.. this in event riding terms is called, my turn, your turn, based on trust respect and understanding.. a true partnership. Welcome to Lady Bell's Lodge.

The evening starts with us welcoming in the Elements, the Directions and the web of life, into our sacred circle. Arniya then dances the energy in with Celestial Energy Movement, for the group. This creates a vortex of Divine power into the middle of the tent. Each person is linked into this Divine power, and receives a "top-up" of Divinity.
We then have an opportunity for each person to hold the Talking Stick and send positive energy to their life, or current experience, or to ask the Divine for help. This is completely optional. Throughout the evening, you will have opportunities to choose oracle cards to support your guidance through life.

At 8pm the Zoom people join our circle. They will get to choose an oracle card and be connected into the vortex of power in the tent. This always creates an energy of expansion within the group.
Arniya then gives a wee run down of any current energies influencing the planet, before she leads everyone on a Journey Meditation. Some weeks we to the V.U soul plane. Sometimes we travel to our inner world. Sometimes the guardians take us somewhere else entirely. Each journey is channelled to support the needs of whoever is present.
After the meditation, we say goodbye to our Zoom friends, close the energy on the circle and give thanks. After this journey is complete, we have a cup of tea - time for a chat or playing with oracle cards, enjoying each other’s company in the uplifted space.

This is normally a fairly jovial group. Sacredness is embraced fully, but not at the expense of a good giggle when it’s called for.

You can choose to join us on a casual basis or join the V.U. program and get dream time support and access to past journey recordings. The V.U is booked monthly. Payment options are below. Click here for more details

Parking up the drive is limited, so please park on the road and walk up if you are able-bodied. Call me if you want me to check if parking is available up the top. 0211412690

long_description:
The Joy of Re-Connection: Using the Organic Self as a resource for Healing
The Joy of Re-Connection: Using the Organic Self as a resource for Healing

A one-and-a-half-day workshop with Lisa Chaplow

Wellington: Fri 27 Nov—Sat 28 Nov 2026

At a time when so much around us can feel uncertain, overwhelming or disconnected, how do we stay connected to what is alive, nourishing and joyful within us?

This workshop invites us to slow down and reconnect with the natural impulse towards wholeness and connection that lives within us all. Through mindful awareness, embodied exploration and the wisdom of the Organic Self, we will explore how healing can also open pathways towards greater vitality, creativity and joy.

Our developmental experiences inevitably include moments of wounding, where our needs are not met sufficiently. In response to this pain, the Self can become fragmented into protective parts that continue to unconsciously shape our sense of who we are and what we can expect from life.

While it is important to understand the origins of these patterns, healing also invites us to reconnect with and re-embody the Organic Self; a powerful source of wisdom and vitality. As we do this, we can free the natural impulse towards wholeness and allow new possibilities for living and relating to emerge. The process of healing can become more effortless, creative and joyful.

In this workshop, drawing on the principles and practices of Hakomi Mindful Somatic Psychotherapy, we will explore:

☆ mindfulness as a way of reconnecting with and embodying the Organic Self.

☆ the body and somatic experience as sources of guidance and wisdom in healing.
ways of supporting the Organic Impulse as a creative and intentional process.

☆ experiencing and celebrating wholeness as a natural state of being.

This is an experiential workshop, offering participants the opportunity to explore the material personally while also developing practical skills for facilitating healing with others. We will explore how the plasticity of the human brain, together with the courage and wisdom of the human heart, can support new neural pathways and possibilities that are more expansive and life-giving.

This workshop meets the pre-requisite requirement for undertaking Hakomi Comprehensive training.

Time and Date:
Friday 27 Nov 2026: 6.00pm – 9.00pm
Saturday 28 Nov 2026: 9.30am – 5.30pm

Venue:

Seatoun, Wellington

Full Fee: $350 (GST incl) thereafter

No refunds will be available after 13.11.26

long_description:
The Crayford Trio @ The RSC

The Crayford Trio, stalwarts of the NZ jazz scene, featuring Miles Crayford on piano & organ, Rory Macartney on Bass, and Greg Crayford leading the group from the drum kit. They will play some of the catchy, original music of Terry Crayford, father to Greg and grandfather to miles, other jazz standards, original music and well-known singalong songs.

Band Members
Miles Crayford – piano, organ
Miles is a third generation pianist from the Crayford family. He draws on both Jazz and Latin-Jazz influences and has spent some time in South America performing. Miles now resides in Kapiti Coast and is focused on playing the hammond organ as well as the piano.

Greg Crayford – drums/guitar/voice, MC
Greg has been performing for more than thirty years as a jazz/show/rock musician in NZ and as support for international acts. Greg’s involvement in musical theatre as musical director/drummer/keyboardist/guitarist/percussionist has included Jesus Christ Superstar, Footloose, West Side Story and Joseph and The Amazing Technicolour Dreamcoat and many more.

Rory Macartney - Bass

Originally from Tauranga New Zealand, and born to a musical family, Rory graduated from Victoria University of Wellington’s NZ School of Music. Post studies he moved to London for several years, continuing to perform, study and work as a sound engineer including at Abbey Road studios.

Rory’s wealth of performing and recording experience includes time on New Zealand and international stages, from the Monterey Jazz Festival to Homegrown to recording at Universal Studio’s. These diverse experiences make him a first call session bass player and band leader.

Cancer Bats (Can)
CANCER BATS (CAN) RETURN TO NZ FOR TWO HUGE SHOWS

Kaitaia Fire and Sticky Fingaz Tour Management present:

Canadian hardcore heavyweights Cancer Bats return to New Zealand in January 2027, bringing their notoriously raucous live show to Wellington’s Valhalla and Auckland’s Whammy — iconic venues where punters can truly throw it down.

Think packed rooms, killer sound, and nowhere to hide when the pit kicks off. The tour comes in support of Cancer Bats’ newly released eighth studio album, Give Me Dirt — a record that delivers the sound the band’s been building towards for more than two decades.

“We’ve been building and working towards this,” says vocalist Liam Cormier about the new album. “Each record that we make is a chance to learn and evolve into better musicians. We are finally in a position to make the best album of our entire career.” Several tracks, including “Stay Stuck” and the title track “Give Me Dirt,” have already become fan favourites — a testament to Cancer Bats’ infectious virtuosity.

Longtime fans can expect plenty of bangers from across the band’s catalogue, too.

With seven albums behind them, Cancer Bats have no shortage of heavy hitters to draw from! From their earliest records through to their newest material, Cancer Bats have built their reputation on fuzzed-out bass and guitar, thunderous drums, and anthemic vocals — music made to be played loud and experienced up close.

If you’ve seen Cancer Bats before, you know what to expect: sweat, volume, flying bodies, and a crowd ready to throw down from the first note to the last.

Helping bring the heat and make the tour a reality is New Zealand’s favourite hot sauce, Kaitaia Fire. See y’all in the pit!

Sunday January 24th, 2027 — Valhalla — Wellington

Doors 8pm, R18 (or with a sober legal guardian)

name: Explore Butterfly Creek
venue: Butterfly Creek, East Harbour Regional Park, Lower Hutt 5013,East Harbour Regional Park, Kowhai St, Eastbourne, Lower Hutt 5013, New Zealand, Lower Hutt
long_description:
Explore Butterfly Creek
Real stories, real fun! Discover a hidden piece of local history and capture a memorable photo in the heart of the forest.

Head to Butterfly Creek in the Northern Forest of East Harbour Regional Park to follow a series of historical signs and uncover the stories behind this special place. Learn how Butterfly Creek got its name, discover the history of the tearoom that once stood in the forest, and find the beautiful butterfly wings among the trees.

Start from the Kōwhai Street entrance and follow the signs through native bush to Butterfly Creek. The walk includes a steep climb, rewarded by beautiful views and a perfect picnic spot at the end.

East Harbour Regional Park is a special place for conservation. Greater Wellington’s work here protects freshwater, restores native bush, and helps build resilience to climate change. Our mana whenua partners and tireless volunteers play a vital role in keeping this park thriving.

Find more Summer Events
We’re hosting free events around the region. For the full programme of events, visit www.gw.govt.nz/events

long_description:
Sing We Nowell
Christmas in Wellington has its own character. Long evenings, pōhutukawa in bloom, the end of the working year in sight, and the anticipation of a well-earned summer break with whānau and friends. The Bach Choir of Wellington invites you to mark the season with an afternoon of festive Christmas music. You can expect the brilliance of voices and the warmth of the brass band coming together in an exciting programme that reflects quiet moments of wonder and all the energy and colour of Christmas. The concert begins with Daniel Pinkham’s Christmas Cantata, drawing on medieval and Renaissance musical motifs full of rhythmic vitality. The music moves from sparkling excitement through moments of mystery, before culminating in an exuberant “Gloria in excelsis Deo”! Bring your singing voice! Alongside the choir and the brass band, you will be invited to join in a selection of our favourite carols, filling the church with Christmas cheer.
Join us for an afternoon of uplifting music, glad tidings, and our special guests, Aotearoa’s leading ,brass ensemble, the Wellington Brass Band!

name: Tea Talks - The power of water. Learn how to bring liquid magic into your life.
venue: Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Tea Talks - The power of water. Learn how to bring liquid magic into your life.
Water was full of life in Egypt. Literally and figuratively. Water flowed through us, as it flowed down the Nile, to meet the flow the the milky way. Each layer mimicking itself (as above, so below).

Current, or flow was an act of God, which was simply a way of naming the invisible forces of nature.

Water also gave life, being the element that helped grow a bountiful harvest. Believing it was alive, you could talk to it, and it would remember and respond. A human characteristic.

Charged and infused waters were used for healing and manifestation (magic). These sacred practices were reimagined and renamed by Christians. Becoming baptism, the flow of water went on to represent rebirth and renewal.

Join me next month to learn about the power of water. Find how using simple and easy practices, you too can bring magic into your life. Tea will also be served.

Mark your calendar now, and I look forward to seeing you there.

Cost of entry: Koha donation

venue: San Fran,171 Cuba Street, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Allegra Krieger
New York based songwriter and composer Allegra Krieger brings her singular blend of folk, rock and indie pop to San Fran on 3 December, joined by special guest Elly Mae.

Known for songwriting that is intimate, understated and deeply observant, Krieger pairs soulful vocals with raw, vulnerable lyricism, moving through themes of love, loss and self-discovery with a striking sense of emotional clarity. Her work has earned praise from the New York Times, who described her as a “deceptively understated songwriter,” while Paste has celebrated the distinctive poetry running through her music.

Having shared stages with artists including Jana Horn, Fust, Johanna Samuels, Shalom and Charlotte Cornfield, Krieger has steadily carved out a space of her own within contemporary indie songwriting, creating music that feels equally at home in moments of quiet reflection and full-band intensity.

Opening the evening is Pōneke songwriter Elly Mae, whose dreamy guitar-led folk-noir draws from the textures of The Brian Jonestown Massacre, PJ Harvey and Mazzy Star. Since first appearing on Wellington stages in early 2025, she has gone on to perform at Newtown Festival, CubaDupa and Flying Nun’s A Month of Saturdays live series, with RNZ describing her sound as a “woozy ethereal slice of dreampop.”

Together, the two artists make for an evening of evocative songwriting, atmospheric guitars and music built around the power of close listening.

Back by some demand! Sloppy Seconds celebrate the 10 year anniversary of the other gig we did.

What is this, you ask? Well. Are you tired of all those slick, polished bands? Tasteless displays of technical virtuosity? "Professionalism?" Look no further than Sloppy Seconds!

It's the band where a hand-picked selection of Wellington's hardest working musicians do a gig on instruments they kind of play. Maybe they learned as a kid, or picked it up for an itinerant job, or maybe even just play for the fun of it!

Here's what people had to say in 2016:

"actually not that bad." - a satisfied punter

Allowed to Birth - Kāpiti Screening
Join us for a special screening of Allowed to Birth, a powerful new documentary exploring birth, choice, autonomy and the importance of respectful maternity care.

long_description:
Young Photographer Award 2026
📸🏆 You're invited to the Young Photographer Awards 2026!

On 2 December, we're bringing our photography community together for a very special evening celebrating the creativity, achievements and talent of young photographers across the Wellington region and beyond.

After a wonderful first event last year, we're excited to make this year's celebration even bigger and more inspiring!

🎟️ The event is FREE and everyone is welcome!

Register here: https://events.humanitix.com/young-photographer-awards-2026

At The Art of Seeing Academy, we run photography workshops for children and teenagers aged 7–18, supported by our amazing tutors and volunteers. Over the past few years, we've delivered more than 300 workshops across schools, weekend programmes, homeschool groups and community events.

We've seen children discover photography for the first time, grow in confidence, develop their creativity and start seeing the world around them in completely new ways. And we couldn't be prouder of them! 💖

🏆 The Awards night is our chance to celebrate their journeys, recognise their efforts and achievements, and showcase their wonderful photographs on the big screen.

🌟 We're also delighted to welcome five professional photographers as guest speakers! They'll share stories from their careers, their creative journeys, challenges and what inspires them. We hope their experiences will inspire not only our young photographers but everyone in the audience.

Last year, around 200 people joined us, and we'd love to see even more familiar and new faces this time!

Whether you're a photographer, a parent, a teacher, a supporter of the arts or simply someone who believes in encouraging young creative minds, we'd love you to be part of this special evening.

Please come along, bring your whānau and friends, and help us celebrate the next generation of photographers! And we'd really appreciate you sharing this event far and wide. ❤️

A huge thank you to Hutt City Council, our sponsors and our wonderful local community for helping make this free event possible.

long_description:
Circle Time
A concert in three circles moving between installation, sound and performance.

About this Event



Curated by composer-artists Elliot Vaughan and Noel Meek, STROMA transforms Massey’s Great Hall into a space for listening, wandering and encountering music from different perspectives.

The evening unfolds in three circles.

From 7:00pm, arrive at your own pace for an open, self-guided installation in the Great Hall. Wander through a collection of intimate works, sounds and performances, taking time to explore the space before gathering at 7:30pm.

At 7:30pm, the space transforms for Gordon Monahan’s Speaker Swinging, as performers set speakers into motion, sending sound and circles of light through the Great Hall.

Then, at approximately 8:00pm, the audience gathers in the round for a seated concert of chamber music, bringing together works by composers from Aotearoa and beyond, including a new commission by Eve de Castro-Robinson.

From open exploration, through sound and movement, to a concert in the round, the evening moves between different ways of listening, experiencing and inhabiting the space.

name: AI Self Defence with Emma Humphrey
venue: Toi Aro,3 Market Ln, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand, Wellington
long_description:
AI Self Defence with Emma Humphrey
AI is now built into the tools we use every day, and the risks are changing faster than traditional security thinking can keep up. This talk is a practical guide to the security, privacy and operational risks that come with modern AI.

We’ll look at how AI systems actually fail and how bad actors exploit them, using recent real-world cases such as the Hugging Face supply-chain breach. You’ll come away understanding the main threats, including prompt injection, data leakage and automated social engineering.
Then we’ll get practical. You’ll leave with “self-defence” strategies you can use straight away:

A simple framework for working out your own personal threat model
How to keep sensitive data out of model training
What to look for when evaluating a vendor’s guardrails
Habits that keep you resilient as the tools keep changing
Whether you’re a developer, a professional, or just curious about tech, this session will help you use AI confidently and safely.

About the speaker

Emma Humphrey is the Director of AI Safety New Zealand. Originally from Christchurch, with a background in physics and mathematics, she spent a decade overseas in data science startups before joining the UK Home Office. There she spent four years leading high-stakes projects in highly secure environments: designing tools to detect deepfakes and criminal exploitation, building digital tools to support sexual assault survivors, and auditing automated hiring systems for hidden bias.

Since returning home, Emma has focused on the non-profit and research space. She organised New Zealand’s inaugural AI Safety Conference and launched the country’s first AI Safety co-working space for researchers and non-profits. Through the Nelson AI Sandbox, she has helped more than 150 non-profits across Christchurch adopt AI safely and save time with the right tools.

name: Manawa Ora Mirimiri - The Foundations of Māori Healing & Bodywork
venue: 236 Middleton Road
long_description:
Manawa Ora Mirimiri - The Foundations of Māori Healing & Bodywork
Experience traditional Māori healing practices grounded in cultural knowledge in this 2-day Foundational workshop with Manawa Ora

About this Event



Nau mai, haere mai ki Manawa Ora – The Foundations of Māori Healing and Bodywork.

We invite you to reconnect with the wisdom of our tūpuna and explore the foundations of traditional Māori healing through a holistic, hands-on approach to wellbeing. Grounded in mātauranga Māori, this workshop provides an introduction to the principles, values and practices that underpin Māori healing.

Throughout this workshop, participants will be introduced to mirimiri and romiromi (Māori bodywork), exploring intention and connection in the healing process. We will consider cultural aspects such as whakapapa, tikanga, manaakitanga and wairuatanga.

The workshop offers a supportive space to learn, reflect and develop an awareness of how Māori healing traditions can inform our approach to wellbeing, both for ourselves and for those we care for. Participants will be encouraged to pay attention to their own bodies, deepen their connection with others and appreciate the responsibility that comes with engaging in the healing process.

Over the last 10 years, these workshops have welcomed people from all races and backgrounds. Wānanga/workshops are safe spaces for people to come together for the pupose of learning and healing, guided by tikanga.

At Manawa Ora, we believe that healing begins with connection – connection to ourselves, to one another, to our whakapapa and to the ancient knowledge of Rongoā Māori passed down through generations.

Whether you are beginning your journey into Māori healing or seeking to strengthen your existing understanding, this workshop provides a foundation from which to grow with respect, aroha and intention.

PLEASE NOTE THIS WORKSHOP IS NOT A QUALIFICATION TO PRACTICE.

The 2-day workshop includes:

Cultural philosophies
Whatumanawa (intuitive diagnosis)
Self-awareness and insight
Waiata, karakia and takutaku
Spiritual hygiene
Introduction to mirimiri and romiromi
Group interaction & hands-on practice
Selfcare and tools to maintain wellness

long_description:
Hey AI, Mark My Words! 🤖 - Free Interactive Writing & AI Workshop
� AI, MARK MY WORDS! - A FREE Writing Workshop

Have you ever asked AI to improve your writing, then wondered whether its suggestions were actually any good? Or found yourself using complicated words just to make your writing sound more professional?

Well, this workshop might be for you!

We're excited to have Kai (Anh Khoa Dang), one of our young Viet Hub NZ volunteers, leading this workshop on 28 November.

Over the past few weeks, Kai has been helping students with their IELTS writing. Through those sessions, he noticed something interesting: many learners were relying on AI-generated answers or trying too hard to use fancy vocabulary, when sometimes the simplest words worked best.

So Kai came up with an idea. Why not get everyone together, write something, ask AI to check it, and then see whether AI actually gets it right?

And that's how "AI, Mark My Words!" came about!

� During the workshop, you'll have a go at writing an email, job application or short essay. You'll learn how to choose the right words, spot common mistakes and test AI's feedback against your own judgement.

It's a hands-on session, so expect plenty of writing, discussions and a bit of friendly competition with AI!

� Saturday, 28 November 2026
� 1:00–3:00 PM
� Te Tai Ohinga Youth Hub, 203 Willis Street, Wellington
� FREE – only 25 places available
� Just bring your phone and curiosity!

The workshop will be in English, with Vietnamese support available if needed. Whether you're a student, preparing for IELTS, applying for jobs or simply wanting to write more confidently, you're welcome to join us.

� One thing we're particularly happy about is seeing Kai take the initiative to plan and lead something of his own.

At Viet Hub NZ, we want young people to feel comfortable sharing their ideas, trying new things and taking on leadership roles. Not every idea has to be perfect from the start. Sometimes, all it takes is someone willing to give it a go and a community willing to support them.

So come along, learn something useful and show Kai some support.

Organised by Viet Hub NZ, with support from Te Tai Ohinga Youth Hub.

#VietHubNZ #AIMarkMyWords #YouthLeadership #WellingtonEvents #CommunityLearning

long_description:
Deep Listening Soundbath at Erskine Chapel
A Deep Listening Soundbath inside the sublime acoustics of Erskine Chapel

$45

Limited door sales for $50

Please bring a yoga mat, pillow, eye mask and blanket - or whatever it is you need to feel most warm and comfortable. Dress comfortably.

Discover the transformative effects of sound therapy with this 1.5hr-hour sound bath experience.

During this session, participants will be surrounded by the resonant vibrations of gongs and taonga pūoro, carefully designed to induce deep states of relaxation and calm. As you settle into the experience, allow the soothing tones to wash over you, releasing tension and promoting a sense of inner peace.

Scientific studies have highlighted the benefits of sound therapy in reducing stress and promoting overall well-being. The rhythmic patterns and overtones of the gongs and other instruments can help entrain brainwaves, leading to a meditative state and improved mental clarity.

Beyond the immediate effects, many participants report experiencing lasting benefits such as improved sleep, reduced anxiety, and enhanced mood following a gong bath session. By immersing yourself in the healing vibrations of the sounds, you can tap into a deeper sense of relaxation and rejuvenation.

Whether you're looking to unwind after a long day or explore new avenues of self-care, this 1.5hr-hour soundbath offers a unique opportunity to reconnect with yourself and find balance amidst the hustle and bustle of daily life. There will be cups of tea available afterwards to help us integrate and ground.

*THIS EVENT IS RESTRICTED TO 40 PEOPLE ONLY**

Disclaimer
Sound baths are safe and supportive for most people. However, please consult your doctor or mental health professional before attending if you:-have a pacemaker or other implanted medical device
-live with epilepsy or a sound-sensitive condition
-are in the first trimester of pregnancy
-are experiencing severe or unmanaged mental health challenges (such as psychosis, schizophrenia, or PTSD)If you have recent injuries, surgeries, or other health concerns, let me know so we can make sure you’re comfortable.

Everyone responds differently to sound. If at any point during the session you feel overwhelmed or uncomfortable, you are welcome to sit up, move gently, or step outside. Your wellbeing always comes first



About Us

Briar Prastiti

Greek–New Zealand composer and vocalist Briar Prastiti is known for her diverse musical practice, spanning contemporary orchestral and chamber music, film, theatre, songwriting, and electronic production. Her most recent compositional project was an epic work for massed choir, solo voice, and taonga pūoro, commissioned for the opening ceremony of Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui, Wellington Central Library. In this work, Briar performed as solo vocalist alongside Alistair Fraser on taonga pūoro.



Alistair Fraser

Alistair is a practitioner of ngā taonga pūoro. He has performed, composed, and collaborated with many of Aotearoa's finest artists, across genres of music and alongside various artistic disciplines since 1999. He worked as a maker, researcher and performer of ngā taonga pūoro nationally and internationally for the past 26 years. He has toured as a soloist with the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra, worked recently with Good Company Arts, Shayne Carter with the Zealand Dance Company for their work Home, Land and Sea, and also for David Long and Stephen Gallagher's score for the Emmy Award winning TV series Secrets at Red Rocks.



Erika Grant

Erika is a musician and astrologer based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. She has 35+ years musical experience, in bands, orchestras and various ensembles. She has created music for film, parades and overnight soundbaths. Erika has an interest in the healing properties of sound for mental and physical wellbeing, which she currently explores through her gong bathing practice

long_description:
AIRHORN HOLIDAY OFFICE PARTY
HAPPY HOLIDAYS FROM AIRHORN!

It's the time of the year for office parties. We tried to do an Airhorn party last year, just the crew, but it was so awkward. Something was missing: all of you! We can't do Airhorn without Audience! We can't even party without Audience! And so, this year, Audience is invited to the Airhorn Office Holiday Party!

Is this a wholesome holiday party mixing it up with audience and comics? Is it an immersive theatre experience? Is it a bold narrative hidden in a casual hangout pretending to be a Christmas comedy show? ¿Por qué no las tres?!

Your Airhorn faves will be here, like Alayne Dick, Zach Mandeville, Anna Maclean, Lesa Macleod-Whiting, Ginge and Minge, Oliver Pol, Joana Joy, and Meaghan Fisher! We're going to put on a party for you to attend! There'll be a white elephant gift exchange!

To be entirely truthful, we booked the theatre at the start of the year and it just said "Airhorn Christmas Party" and we truly could not remember if this was for an actual party or an actual show. The irony and artifice is getting too much. We cannot tell where the stage ends, what is personal and what is performance. And so we are just leaning into it.

It's a party! It's a show! It's both! Sincerely celebrate the end of year with Airhorn!

We are ALSO experimenting with new ticket style. It is now PAY WHAT YOU CAN! So the ticket is free, with a donation amount that you can enter in. No combos, no early bird deals, just whatever you'd like to pay!

long_description:
Wellington Perinatal Network
A causal meet-up and networking event for professionals working in the perinatal space in greater Wellington.

About this Event


Join the Wellington Perinatal Network.




Our final hui for 2026! Come and join us for a celebratory-style catch up to end the year at the Pātaka Art + Museum in Porirua.

And as a little something extra special, our network member Maddie from Milestone Photography is going to bring along her camera and set up a little Christmas-inspired corner so we can grab some lovely seasonal pics! Thank you Maddie!

.............................................................................................................................................................................

Do you work with or offer services to whānau who are pregnant or postpartum? Would you like to learn more about the variety of support available for your clients in their community, plus expand your professional network too?

You are invited to join the Wellington Perinatal Network. An informal, professional network of practitioners working with folks who are having, who have had, or are in the thick of raising pēpi and tamariki.

Whatever you offer - whether birth preparation/education, lactation consultancy, pelvic physio, chiropractic, massage therapy, doula services, infant massage courses or mental health services (plus the many other talented and valued perinatal offerings in our community) - come along and share your knowledge and passion with a view to increased collaboration in this space.

Each event features a couple of short introductory talks from practitioners based in the Wellington region, plus the chance to introduce yourself and your mahi, plus share ideas and experiences with other like-minded practitioners.

venue: 272 Taranaki Street, New Zealand 6001,272 Taranaki St, Mount Cook, Wellington 6011, New Zealand, Wellington
long_description:
Jan-Bas Bolen (Netherlands) | DSLB
A child prodigy on the violin, Amsterdam's Jan-Bas Bolen eschewed the world of professional classical music in favour of electronic music and the radical autonomy of the inventor. "I spent at least 5000 hours in the electronic Stockhausen Studio in The Hague" Bolen says, "learning how to patch, learning how to build circuitry.” He also wanted to perform his electronic works live, but was confronted with the limitations of existing interfaces such as keyboards and mixing desks, a situation which would eventually lead him to the HyperTheremin.

The HyperTheremin is a touchless, magical instrument, that allows for the creation of sonic and visual poetry through manual control of invisible drivers, revealed only by a precise choreography of the hands in space. A worthy accomplice of the original Theremin, Bolen's instrument incorporates touch-less ('non-haptic') technologies from the game industry, to add sliders and switches in a virtual, 4-dimensional console.

https://jbbollen.net/hypertheremin/
-
DSLB is the solo project of Chrissie Butler, a showcase for a love of long endings and the hum things make when you hold them close to your ear. DSLB is an improvised mash-up of ancient record players, purring keyboards, kitchen utensils and found objects. Recordings are released by skirted Records.

https://skirtedrecords.com/dslb/

Together by Design
Good food, warm company and big ideas, this one’s for you

On Thursday 26 November, we’re gathering at the beautiful Te Ahumairangi Foyer at the National Library in Thorndon for an evening that’s equal parts night out and invitation to shape what comes next.

This is Together by Design, a chance to connect, unwind and have your say in where Women of Pōneke goes from here. We’ll be joined by Kathryn Robinson and Celine Yockney from Verian (formerly Colmar Brunton), who’ve generously brought their research and engagement expertise to help design the evening. The questions are the kind you’d happily explore over a glass of wine, what do you value most about this community, what should we protect as we grow, and where do you want to see us go?

Expect nourishing platters from our friends at Everybody Eats, wine from Luna Estate, and the kind of conversation that happens when good people are in the room together.

Come with friends. Come on your own and leave having met someone new. All are welcome.

long_description:
Auditions: The Beauty Queen of Leenane
Come audition for our first show of 2027!

The Beauty Queen of Leenane
📖 Written by Martin McDonagh
🎭 Directed by Ewen Coleman

Production dates– 7-17 April 2027

Set in the mountains of Connemara, County Galway, in the early 1990’s, The Beauty Queen of Leenane tells the darkly comic tale of Maureen Folan, a plain and lonely woman in her early 40s, and Mag, her manipulative aging mother, whose interference in Maureen’s first and possibly final chance of a loving relationship sets in motion a train of events that leads inexorably towards the play’s terrifying dénouement.

The Beauty Queen of Leenane is described as a dark comedy thriller with an excruciating clash of characters locked in a plot that is equal parts funny, sad and violent as the story of a grown-up daughter whose dreams are thwarted by the demands of a cantankerous mother slowly unfolds.

Cast

Maureen Folan, 40 plus. A plain looking spinster who has spent all her life care for her mother which she deeply regrets

Mag, her 70-year-old mother. A cantankerous old biddy who, although frail, still has some of the fire of her youth

Pato Dooley – 40 plus. A strikingly handsome local who takes a shine to Maureen

Ray Dooley, 19. Pato’s younger brother, a bit of a mischievous rascal around town

If interested in auditioning please complete an audition form via our website- https://manalittletheatre.org.nz/auditions/

For further details and a script contact the director Ewen Coleman –

long_description:
Kaitoke Amazing Race
Real teamwork, real fun! Gather your crew and see if you can conquer the Kaitoke Amazing Race.

Register a team and put your problem-solving, teamwork, and outdoor skills to the test in this fun-filled family challenge. Navigate your way around Kaitoke Regional Park, visiting checkpoints and completing as many activities as you can before time runs out.

Every checkpoint offers a new opportunity to work together, think on your feet, and have fun along the way. Explore the beauty of Kaitoke Regional Park, discover new corners of the park, and have fun together.

Kaitoke Regional Park is home to ancient forest, peaceful walking tracks, and the upper reaches of Te Awa Kairangi/Hutt River. Greater Wellington works to protect and restore this special place, helping native plants and wildlife thrive while providing opportunities for people to connect with nature. Our mana whenua partners, volunteers, and park teams play an important role in caring for this treasured landscape.

Register your team by clicking on the link now - https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/DyrESLhQXE


Find more Summer Events
We’re hosting free events around the region. For the full programme of events, visit www.gw.govt.nz/events

Proudly supported by Wellington City Council.

name: Night Shift: Feeling Our Way Towards the Future
venue: City Gallery Wellington,Data Security Services, Harris St, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand, Wellington
long_description:
Night Shift: Feeling Our Way Towards the Future
What does the future feel like?

Night Shift brings short talks, exhibition tours, and hands-on activities inspired by the world of Cornelia Parker to three Thursday evenings.

Come with friends or on your own, explore at your own pace, and linger over a drink at āta.

Join two Aotearoa writers whose fiction ventures into the unknown: Pip Adam, winner of the 2026 Ursula K. Le Guin Prize for Fiction, and Terri Te Tau, author of The Valley of Unlikely Acquaintances and member of the artist collective Mataaho.

With titles like The Future (Sixes & Sevens) and Through a Glass Darkly, Cornelia Parker’s artworks swirl with the sense that nothing is quite settled. Crawl inside that feeling with us.

--

Programme

5.30pm & 7.30pm: Exhibition Tours
Take a closer look at Cornelia Parker on a 45-minute guided tour. First come, first served.

5.30pm, 6.15pm, 7pm, 7.45pm: Step Inside the Darkroom
The Handmade Darkroom Collective is taking over our classroom and turning it into a working photographic darkroom. Inspired by Cornelia Parker, you are invited to make your own photogram, playing with directional light and objects of significance or visual interest. Feel free to bring along some small trinkets you may wish to print with.

Each time slot has a 16-person capacity, on a first-in-first-served basis. Please queue at the Taupuni Toi Education Studio (upstairs) before the session you wish to attend.

6.15pm & 6.45pm: Feeling Our Way Towards the Future
Two short talks with writers Pip Adam and Terri Te Tau, inspired by Cornelia Parker.

7.00–8.00pm: Behind the Scenes: Cornelia Parker
How do you hang an explosion? Meet some of the people who installed the exhibition and care for its artworks. Drop in, ask questions and find out what it takes to bring this exhibition to life.

--
Tickets Required

2-for-1 Tickets
Adult $25
Concession $22

id: Mozart Requiem (Duncan Druce Completion)-Te Raukura ki Kāpiti,32 Raumati Rd, Raumati Beach, Paraparaumu 5032, New Zealand, Paraparaumu-All Events In
name: Mozart Requiem (Duncan Druce Completion)
venue: Te Raukura ki Kāpiti,32 Raumati Rd, Raumati Beach, Paraparaumu 5032, New Zealand, Paraparaumu
long_description:
Mozart Requiem (Duncan Druce Completion)
Kāpiti Chorale and Capital Choir join forces with orchestra and soloists for a powerful performance of Mozart's final masterpiece.

When Mozart died in 1791 at the age of 35, he left the Requiem unfinished. Within months, his student Franz Xaver Süssmayr completed the work on behalf of Mozart's widow Constanze. His version became one of the most famous and beloved works in the choral repertoire and remains the version most often performed today.

Yet Mozart's surviving sketches continued to raise questions. For more than 200 years, composers and scholars have revisited them, searching for clues to how Mozart himself intended to complete the work.

This concert presents one of the most fascinating answers to that question: the Duncan Druce completion. Created in 1984 by the English composer, performer and musicologist Duncan Druce, it draws on Mozart's surviving manuscript while revisiting parts of the traditional completion. The result offers a fresh perspective on one of the defining works of the classical repertoire.

This special collaboration brings together the combined forces of Kāpiti Chorale and Capital Choir, four outstanding soloists and orchestra for two performances: Saturday 28 November at Te Raukura ki Kapiti, Paraparaumu, and Saturday 5 December at the Riley Centre, Wellington High School.

The programme opens with a diverse selection of choral music, including works by Mozart, Salieri, Haydn, Princess Te Rangi Pai and William Dawson, before culminating in Mozart's Requiem.

Soloists

Barbara Paterson, soprano
Ruth Armishaw, alto
Richard Taylor, tenor
Joseph Haddow, bass

- For accessibility seating information and wheelchair space bookings please email or call 04)9740535 during office hours.
- Door sales are only available if the event doesn't sell out prior.

This collaboration will be presented in both Kāpiti and Wellington.
https://www.eventfinda.co.nz/tours-festivals/2026/mozart-requiem

Duration: Approximately 2 hours including interval.

Step into Tide and Tempest, an original production loosely inspired by Shakespeare’s The Tempest and the classic folktale The Magician’s Apprentice.

long_description:
Oneiric Reality: The architecture of a dream | Art exhibition
‘Oneiric Reality | The architecture of a dream’ is what it feels like to live between two worlds: the one you come from and the one you’ve built. Some of it feels like a dream, some of it feels like home, and some of it feels like both at once. For three days, both live in the same room.

A kind of lucid dream: knowing you’re inside it, and discovering you can choose what comes next.

Work by Latin American artists and artists of Latin heritage from across Aotearoa: paint, ink, photographs, collage, poems. Not all of it is dreamlike. All of it was made from somewhere in between.

Fri 27 Nov: opening night, 7:30 pm

Sat 28 Nov: 11 am to 2 pm and 5 pm to 8 pm

Sun 29 Nov: 12 pm to 3 pm

Come as you are. Wander in any direction. 🌀

GET YOUR TICKETS HERE
https://events.humanitix.com/oneiric-reality-the-architecture-of-a-dream-or-art-exhibition

Agenda:

🌀 Friday 27 Nov

5:30 pm - 6:30 pm | Blackout Poetry workshop
Blackout poetry is the mindful act of removing, reshaping and reimagining words. During this 1-hour workshop, you will take a page, choose the words that speak to you, and cross out the rest, until an ordinary text becomes something that’s entirely yours. No writing experience is needed.
This is a paid event. More info https://events.humanitix.com/blackout-poetry-workshop-at-oneiric-dream-or-the-architecture-of-a-dream-exhibition

7:30 pm | Gallery opening
Gallery opening is on Friday 27 Nov, from 7:30 pm. There’ll be wine and artists to meet, and heaps of them are showing their work for the first time. Come say hola!

🌀 Saturday 28 Nov

5:00 pm - 6:00 pm | Express tarot readings
In a dream you can’t always steer, but in real life you can. Pull a card and find out what the tarot says you could do to make your reality feel more like yours. For fun, and maybe a little self-reflection.

long_description:
NZ Art Show
The NZ Art Show is Aotearoa's premier weekend showcasing original art, where the vibrant culture of art, people, and city converge. Held annually at the TSB Bank Arena in Wellington, this event transforms the waterfront into a celebration of New Zealand art. Artists and art enthusiasts gather for an unforgettable experience that spans one evening and three days during the King's Birthday Weekend. This inclusive event caters to everyone, from novice collectors to lifelong art lovers, featuring a diverse array of original works and the opportunity to meet the artists behind them.

With over 200 artists presenting more than 4,000 artworks, the NZ Art Show attracts around 15,000 visitors each year. Attendees can explore curated spaces that highlight various facets of Aotearoa’s creative community, including sculpture, photography, and urban expression. Notable collaborations, such as those with Emerging contemporary Toi Māori voices and Toi Rauwhārangi from Massey University, celebrate the next generation of Māori artists. The show also includes the People’s Choice Art Award, where visitors can vote for their favorite artwork, with a $3,000 prize awarded to the winning artist, sponsored by Urban Relics. This platform supports emerging artists on their professional journeys, transforming reclaimed urban materials into captivating contemporary pieces that explore themes of memory and place.

The NZ Art Show's vision is to ensure that every New Zealander has the opportunity to own an original New Zealand artwork. Since its inception in 2004, this event has played a pivotal role in shaping the art market in Aotearoa, with profits reinvested into the arts community to foster creativity at all levels. The show provides comfortable lounge spaces throughout the venue for attendees to relax and recharge, enhancing the overall experience. With a country ranking of 57, the NZ Art Show stands out in the annual calendar of art events, making it a must-visit for anyone interested in the rich tapestry of New Zealand's artistic landscape.

long_description:
Distilled Comedy
4 Weeks to Christmas ... WTF - if I wasn't laughing, I'd be crying ... fortunately we have a great night of comedy to help with that.

Welcome to the comedy open mic that politely asks structure to wait outside while we set fire to it.

This is the Home of The Jar — our slightly unhinged, deeply democratic system where the audience randomly selects who goes up next. No lineups. No pecking order. No sacred cows. Just brave humans, questionable decisions, and whatever name comes out of the jar. It’s equal parts comedy show, social experiment, and mild psychological thriller.

You might see a first-timer stepping up for their debut. You might see a seasoned comic testing fresh material. You might see someone absolutely smash it. You might see someone realise, in real time, that jokes are harder than they look. That’s the magic.

Come in from the cooler autumn air, grab some food, sip a cocktail, and settle in. The room fills fast, the energy builds quicker, and being there from the start means you’re fully invested when the jar starts causing trouble.

If you love comedy in its rawest, most unpredictable form — this is your night.
If you’ve ever thought, “I could probably do that” — the jar would love to meet you.

Cheap laughs. Big vibes. Absolute chaos.

long_description:
The Waffleathon – 24 Hours of Walking, Talking & Waffling
🚶‍♂️☕ THE WAFFLEATHON – 24 HOURS OF WALKING, TALKING & WAFFLING! ❤️

Walk a little. Talk a lot. Nobody walks alone.

Kia ora everyone! I'm Durry, founder of The Bro Circle with Durry.

This Movember, I'm taking on something I've never done before.

I'm walking for 24 hours around Wellington and the Hutt Valley to raise awareness and funds for men's health, especially men's mental health.

Why?

Because I've had my own battles with mental health. I know what it's like when life gets bloody hard, and I know how much difference one conversation can make.

But here's the thing.

Mental health is serious. Talking about it doesn't always have to be.

Sometimes all we need is a walk, a coffee, a laugh or someone willing to listen.

And that's what The Waffleathon is all about!

📅 SATURDAY 28 NOVEMBER – SUNDAY 29 NOVEMBER 2026

⏰ 6AM – 6AM (24 HOURS)

📍 START & FINISH:
Bottom of Wainui Hill car park, Wainuiomata side.

🗺️ WHERE ARE WE WALKING?

We'll start in Wainuiomata, head through Petone, into Wellington and around Mount Victoria, before making our way back through the Hutt Valley, towards Upper Hutt and eventually home to Wainuiomata.

The route is flexible, and we'll adjust it depending on the weather, conditions and how everyone's travelling.

☕ CONFIRMED FIRST COFFEE STOP

The Flying Bean – Petone Beach
Saturday 28 November, 8AM.

Come meet us for a coffee, a yarn or join us for part of the walk!

More community meetup locations and approximate times will be announced as we get closer.

❤️ WHO CAN JOIN?

EVERYONE!

Bring your mates, your family, your kids or your dog.

Walk for 10 minutes, an hour, or as long as you like.

You don't have to walk the full 24 hours.

You don't even have to talk about mental health.

Come for a coffee, have a laugh, share a story or simply enjoy being around good people.

There's no pressure and no expectations.

Just people connecting with people.

❤️ WHY I'M WALKING

I walk for 24 hours because some people have been walking through darkness for years — and nobody should have to walk alone.

We're not just growing moustaches. We're growing conversations, connections, and a community where nobody has to pretend they're okay.

🙌 WANT TO HELP?

I'm organising this event myself, and I'd love support from the community.

Whether you want to walk, volunteer, help with supplies, share the event or support the fundraising, it all makes a difference.

A huge thank you to the businesses, organisations and individuals already getting behind The Waffleathon. I'll be sharing more about our supporters as things are confirmed.

💙 DONATE OR SUPPORT MY MOVEMBER FUNDRAISER:

https://nz.movember.com/mospace/15544781

🗺️ PLANNED WALKING ROUTE:

https://maps.app.goo.gl/xsrRAZ2XMBBDhcyX6

Please note the route is a guide and may change.

And if you're a local business keen to help, please get in touch!

This isn't about how far we walk.

It's about how many conversations we start, how many connections we make, and reminding people they're not alone.

No judgment. No mask.

Humans Helping Humans ❤️

Let's walk, talk and waffle for a bloody good cause!

Durry
The Bro Circle with Durry

#TheWaffleathon #TheBroCircle #Movember2026 #MensMentalHealth #HumansHelpingHumans

name: Whānau Fishing Day - Ōwhiro Bay
venue: Capital Trout Centre, Landfill Road, Ōwhiro Bay, Wellington 6023,38 Landfill Rd, Owhiro Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand, Wellington
long_description:
Whānau Fishing Day - Ōwhiro Bay
Enjoy a day of trout fishing for the kids, delicious food and refreshments, and a little Christmas cheer while connecting with other local families in a relaxed and welcoming environment.


Parent to Parent Wellington, with support from the Wellington Flyfishers Club, invites you to the Capital Trout Centre in Ōwhiro Bay. The whole family is welcome to attend, although fishing is for children only. Experienced instructors will be on hand to help young anglers learn the ropes, making this a great opportunity for children to try something new and have fun outdoors. Food and refreshments will be provided, and fish can be gutted on-site for a gold coin donation if required.


Please note that the venue includes an open body of water, so parents and caregivers must supervise their children at all times, including those who are not fishing. Numbers are limited and registration is essential, so be sure to register to secure your place and send your details to Jack. We look forward to sharing a memorable day with you and your whānau.


This fun-filled Whānau Fishing Day is being brought to you by IHC Wellington.


Contact Jack Baigent for more information:
| 027 808 3952
